recent_posts.title: How to sell your WordPress aggregator site as an AI agent data feed
recent_posts.summary: WordPress aggregator sites have an untapped second revenue stream: selling curated RSS feeds to AI agent builders. AI models have knowledge cutoffs and need fresh, niche-specific data feeds, which is exactly what aggregator sites already produce. The post outlines how to monetize this by gating premium category feeds with token-based access, white-labeling hubs for agencies, selling entire sites as knowledge assets, or running your own AI data pipeline. A step-by-step guide covers source selection, feed aggregation with WP RSS Aggregator, aggressive curation for AI (agents don't skim like humans), gating feeds via Cloudflare or PHP tokens, and common pitfalls like selling the firehose instead of curated subsets or pricing per request instead of flat monthly.

recent_posts.title: How to Build a WooCommerce Wholesale Store with B2BKing
recent_posts.summary: A step-by-step guide to building a WooCommerce wholesale store using the B2BKing Pro plugin. Covers setting shop mode (B2B-only vs hybrid), creating customer groups (Retailers and Distributors), restricting pricing from guest visitors, configuring trade registration with manual approval and VAT fields, setting group-specific and tiered wholesale pricing, adding a bulk order form, and creating dynamic rules for free shipping and volume discounts. Also touches on subaccounts and purchase lists for repeat buyers.

recent_posts.title: WordPress Media Library Organization No Longer Needs Three Plugins
recent_posts.summary: Infinite Uploads now consolidates WordPress media library management into a single plugin by adding folder organization, granular sorting (8 options), and enhanced search with six filters. Previously, WordPress site owners needed separate plugins for cloud offloading, folder structure, and improved search. The solution supports unlimited nested folders, drag-and-drop, bulk actions, and a migrator for FileBird and HappyFiles is coming. Priced at $19/month with unlimited sites, it targets agencies managing multiple client sites.

recent_posts.title: How responsive images work in WordPress and where the default setup falls short
recent_posts.summary: WordPress has supported responsive images since version 4.4, automatically generating multiple size variants and adding srcset/sizes attributes to img tags. However, the default setup has notable gaps: themes must properly support srcset, the sizes attribute may not reflect actual layout widths, retina/high-DPI displays need 2x variants WordPress doesn't generate, and no compression is applied to size variants. The post explains how srcset and sizes work together, covers edge cases like browser inconsistencies and layout shift prevention via width/height attributes, and recommends plugins like Perfect Images for retina support and ShortPixel for compression and adaptive image serving based on real container dimensions.

recent_posts.title: WordPress Performance Audit: How to Find What’s Slowing Down Your Site
recent_posts.summary: A step-by-step WordPress performance audit guide using four free tools: Google Search Console for real field data on Core Web Vitals, PageSpeed Insights for diagnosing TTFB, render-blocking resources, LCP, and TBT issues, GTmetrix for waterfall analysis to understand loading sequences, and Query Monitor for server-side database query and HTTP API call profiling. The guide concludes with a prioritized action sequence: fix hosting first, then images, then code/caching, and finally third-party scripts.

recent_posts.title: WordPress SEO plugins that use AI in 2026 compared
recent_posts.summary: A practical comparison of seven WordPress SEO plugins that genuinely use AI beyond simple API calls. Covers full-suite options including Yoast SEO Premium, AIOSEO, SEOPress, Rank Math, and Prime SEO, plus Link Whisper as a specialist internal linking add-on. Each plugin is evaluated on its actual AI capabilities, pricing, and ideal use case. Standout differentiators include Prime SEO's AI crawler management for GPTBot and ClaudeBot, Rank Math's competitor content analysis, AIOSEO's E-E-A-T author profiles, and SEOPress's bring-your-own-API-key model. Includes a decision guide matching plugin choices to specific user profiles from solo bloggers to agencies.

recent_posts.title: All-in-One WP Migration Pro Review: The Simplest Way to Move a WordPress Site
recent_posts.summary: All-in-One WP Migration Pro is a WordPress plugin that packages an entire site (database, media, themes, plugins) into a single file for export and import without requiring FTP, database clients, or wp-config.php edits. The Pro version costs $99/year for up to 50 sites (counted by usage, not installs), removes PHP upload size limits via chunked imports, adds 15+ cloud storage integrations, scheduled backups with incremental transfers, WP-CLI support, and a Reset Hub. Key limitations include incompatibility with some popular managed hosts (Kinsta, WP Engine) and certain plugins like Cloudflare and Really Simple SSL during migration. The free version covers most basic migrations, while Pro is best suited for large sites, agencies, or those needing automated cloud backups.

recent_posts.title: WordPress Image SEO Checklist: What Google Actually Looks For
recent_posts.summary: A practical checklist focused on the discoverability layer of WordPress image SEO, covering signals Google uses to find and rank images. Topics include image sitemaps (especially for CDN-hosted images), file naming conventions, declaring width/height to prevent CLS, handling the LCP image correctly (no lazy loading, fetchpriority="high"), writing accurate alt text or automating it with AI tools, captions, structured data for products and recipes, and using Google Search Console's Core Web Vitals report rather than just PageSpeed Insights for real-world validation.

recent_posts.title: 8 practical ways to speed up your WordPress site
recent_posts.summary: A practical guide to improving WordPress site speed, covering the eight highest-impact areas: choosing the right hosting, using an all-in-one performance plugin (FastPixel), dedicated image optimization (ShortPixel), correct lazy loading configuration, plugin auditing, CDN setup, database cleanup, and ongoing measurement. The guide emphasizes starting with Google PageSpeed Insights to identify actual problems, prioritizing hosting, caching, and image optimization as the top three levers, and treating site speed as an ongoing maintenance habit rather than a one-time fix.

recent_posts.title: Modular DS Review: The All-in-One WordPress Maintenance Platform for Agencies and Freelancers
recent_posts.summary: Modular DS is a cloud-based WordPress maintenance platform designed for agencies and freelancers managing multiple client sites. It consolidates updates, backups, uptime monitoring, security scanning, database optimization, and client reporting into a single dashboard. Key features include Update Copilot (AI-powered risk scoring for updates), Safe Updates with before/after screenshot comparison and rollback, Smart Automated Updates with configurable rules, Patchstack-powered vulnerability scanning with early disclosure alerts, and branded client maintenance reports. Pricing spans four tiers (Freelance to Enterprise) with flexible overage to avoid forced tier upgrades. A Patch and Protect add-on applies virtual PHP-level patches before official fixes are released. The platform receives near-perfect ratings on WordPress.org, G2, and Trustpilot, with users praising its convenience and support quality.

top_posts.title: Why WordPress still dominates in 2026 despite better alternatives
top_posts.summary: WordPress continues to dominate 43% of the web in 2026 not because of superior technology, but due to its massive plugin ecosystem of 60,000+ extensions and decades of community knowledge. After evaluating alternatives like static site generators (Astro, Hugo), modern PHP CMSs (Statamic, Craft), headless options (Strapi, Contentful), and hosted builders (Squarespace, Webflow), none offer a true replacement for most use cases. Static generators lack user-friendly dashboards for non-technical clients. Modern CMSs have elegant architecture but tiny ecosystems and limited developer availability. Headless solutions are overengineered for typical websites. Shopify succeeded in e-commerce by being opinionated and fully hosted. The 2024-2025 governance drama between Automattic and WP Engine exposed centralization risks, but no viable alternative has emerged. AI tools may eventually level the playing field by making custom development faster, potentially reducing the plugin ecosystem advantage. For now, WordPress remains the practical default for content-managed sites requiring non-technical editing, despite its aging codebase and divided community over Gutenberg.

top_posts.title: The 60/30/10 Rule Made Our Website Designs Infinitely Better
top_posts.summary: The 60/30/10 rule is a time-tested principle in design that suggests dividing color usage into three distinct proportions. The rule promotes a visually appealing balance in your design, creating a hierarchy that guides the user’s eye through the content. It originated from the interior design world but has been applied in web design to great effect.

top_posts.title: Better Block Editor Review: A Lightweight Block Editor Companion for Next-Level Responsive Design
top_posts.summary: Better Block Editor is a free WordPress plugin that extends the native Block Editor with responsive controls, animations, and hover effects without requiring custom CSS. It adds breakpoint-specific settings for layouts, visibility controls for different screen sizes, and customizable navigation collapse points. The plugin maintains content portability by building on core WordPress blocks rather than proprietary components, making it suitable for developers who want enhanced responsive design capabilities while staying within the WordPress ecosystem. It includes site templates and works with any Block theme.

top_posts.title: Headless Hostman Review: An Easy Way to Make a Static WordPress Website
top_posts.summary: Headless Hostman is a tool that allows you to convert your dynamic WordPress site into a static one while retaining the ability to manage content via the familiar WordPress dashboard. This setup offers benefits such as faster loading times, enhanced security, and easier scalability. The service provides a dedicated hosting environment, utilizes Cloudflare for optimal performance and uptime, and features a straightforward setup. Pricing starts at $125 per month, and although there’s no documentation, customer support is available via a ticketing model.

top_posts.title: Optimize Your WordPress Site with CompressX Image Compression Plugin
top_posts.summary: CompressX is a WordPress plugin designed to enhance website speed by automatically converting and compressing images into WebP and AVIF formats. With its user-friendly features, it offers control over quality and compression levels, supports bulk conversion, and allows auto-resizing upon upload. The plugin is free, making it an excellent solution for optimizing images without impacting their quality.
